data.description:
## Description
**What**: Add a deterministic critic script to dso:story-decomposer that enforces three checks against the structured signals from draft-2: (a) each declared producer surface appears in the named producer story body and each consumer detection appears in the named consumer story body; (b) for every canonical_name with a corresponding plugins/dso/docs/contracts/<canonical_name>.md, the producer-side surface and consumer-side detection both match the contract doc's canonical_surface field; (c) cross-story edges are derived by matching consumes_signals.canonical_name against emits_signals.canonical_name. Each check emits a machine-distinguishable gate identifier on failure ("drift" for check (a), "canonical-anchor" for check (b), and the sc-4 post-pass emits "heuristic-undeclared-signal") rather than a single opaque critic-error, so downstream regression tests can assert which gate fired. On the f360-3a5b pre-fix fixture the critic emits the drift gate identifier and refuses to emit until surfaces are reconciled.
**Why**: This is the producer/consumer signaling-core enforcement that closes the original false-positive gap.
**Scope**:
- IN: the deterministic critic script; the three checks (a)/(b)/(c); a machine-distinguishable gate identifier per check (drift, canonical-anchor); the canonical_surface anchor against contract docs; cross-story edge derivation by canonical_name match; refuse-to-emit behavior keyed to the firing gate identifier; the f360-3a5b pre-fix fixture used to prove refusal.
- OUT: the heuristic zero-declaration post-pass (draft-5, which emits the heuristic-undeclared-signal identifier); the inline field schema (draft-2); preplanning fan-in (draft-4).

## Done Definitions

- Check (a) emits a critic failure tagged with the gate identifier "drift" when a declared producer surface is absent from the named producer story body or a consumer detection is absent from the named consumer story body ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Check (b) emits a critic failure tagged with the gate identifier "canonical-anchor" when a producer surface or consumer detection diverges from the canonical_surface field of the matching plugins/dso/docs/contracts/<canonical_name>.md ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Check (c) derives a cross-story edge by matching a consumes_signals.canonical_name to an emits_signals.canonical_name across the drafted stories ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Each of the three gates emits a distinct machine-readable gate identifier (drift, canonical-anchor, and the sc-4 post-pass heuristic-undeclared-signal) so a consumer can tell which gate fired without parsing prose ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Fed the f360-3a5b pre-fix fixture, the critic emits the drift gate identifier and the decomposer refuses to emit until the surfaces are reconciled ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic, including one test per check, one asserting the three gate identifiers are pairwise distinct, and the f360 refusal case ← Satisfies: sc-2

## Considerations

- [Determinism] The critic is a deterministic script, not an LLM judgment; the original failure mode was prompt-directive enforcement that drifted.
- [Self-reference] The f360-3a5b pre-fix fixture must encode the producer copy-story / consumer copy:needed mismatch that the real f360 epic shipped with.
- [Coupling] Check (b) reads canonical_surface from draft-1's contract docs; if no contract doc exists for a canonical_name, check (b) is skipped for that name and only checks (a)/(c) apply.
- [Gate-identifiers] Each check emits a stable machine-distinguishable gate identifier (drift, canonical-anchor; the sc-4 post-pass emits heuristic-undeclared-signal) instead of a single opaque critic-error, so draft-6's distinct-gate regression assertion is mechanically verifiable. Treat these identifier strings as a contract draft-6 depends on; do not rename without updating the regression fixtures.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a DSO plugin maintainer, I want a deterministic decomposer critic enforcing three signal-coherence checks that refuses to emit on the f360-3a5b fixture, so that producer/consumer surface mismatches are blocked at decomposition time.
